claims.answer: The public download table offers macOS 13+ Intel/Apple Silicon, Windows x64 and Linux AppImage/deb desktop clients. The self-hosted service serves the Air console and task/chat web interface, opened locally at localhost or at an authenticated reachable host address. The README links an official Android APK and an iPhone/iPad App Store client for the user MultiCC server; it notes that iOS availability follows Apple review. A product-owned ./multicc service manager exposes start/update and other service operations. The Air console creates tasks and the task-chat UI sends requests and answers pending decisions.

sources.title: MultiCC: README.md
sources.locator: Download MultiCC; Choose how to work; Quick Start; FAQ
sources.finding: Documents public desktop installers, Android APK and iOS App Store link, standalone setup, local browser UI and self-hosted workspaces. The host/service must stay running.

sources.title: MultiCC: docs/features.md
sources.locator: Multi-provider support, Session orchestration, Task board, Long-running & scheduled work, dashboard and Git worktree management
sources.finding: The feature reference gives exact terminal/chat launch modes, per-task state/worktrees, Commander dispatch, cron and event triggers, syntax-gated merges and Git actions.

sources.title: MultiCC: docs/cli-switching.md
sources.locator: Supported CLIs table and Chat sessions only; switching and native session reuse
sources.finding: Documents Claude Code via Agent SDK in chat and CLI in terminal, Codex exec/app-server, and OpenCode run integration. Each engine retains its own native session, with a bounded visible handoff checkpoint.

sources.title: MultiCC: src/cli-adapters/index.js
sources.locator: createCliAdapters, imports and provider list; createAgyAdapter
sources.finding: The pinned registry wires concrete Gemini, Grok, Pi and Antigravity command adapters as well as the older documented engines. This is a source snapshot; the older multi-CLI table is not a complete current list.

sources.title: MultiCC: docs/configuration.md
sources.locator: Official providers and accounts; provider configuration files
sources.finding: Claude and Codex have official account routes using local CLI login or separately stored accounts; provider stores also accept API credentials. The local CLI login uses the existing login on the host.

sources.title: MultiCC: docs/super-agent.md
sources.locator: From a goal to a result; What ships today; Hosting, access and cost; boundaries
sources.finding: MultiCC supplies Commander and cross-session dispatch, returning async results. Independent tasks can run concurrently; same-shell work is serial and shares a worktree. The workspace is self-hosted on the user computer/server and depends on a running host.

sources.title: MultiCC: docs/router-tools.md
sources.locator: Task-first dispatch tools and sync/async dispatch contracts
sources.finding: The product router tools connect caller and delegated task identities, execute cross-session work and return or wake results. They establish product-owned delegation rather than merely displaying a CLI subagent.

sources.title: MultiCC: public/chat-diff.js
sources.locator: open/select file; renderPatch and paintPatch, especially lines 851-863
sources.finding: The task/session chat diff dock fetches a selected file patch and displays it through renderDiff, falling back to a monospace pre whose textContent is the actual patch. It is a code-content UI, not just an API or file-count list.

sources.title: MultiCC: LICENSE
sources.finding: The main repository grants MIT use, copying and modification free of charge.

sources.title: MultiCC: docs/desktop.md
sources.locator: Desktop app platform table; desktop-vs-CLI differences
sources.finding: Desktop shells ship for macOS, Windows and Linux. The desktop backend binds loopback; remote/LAN access uses the standalone service. Its client and service scope must remain distinct.
